forecaster_note: Offshore for a while in the morning for some clean head high surf at the south exposures and small to fun sized stuff elsewhere for those that want to cruise. Another south wind switch will move through about 10am with onshore lumpy and building surf for the rest of the day. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: Light SW offshore now — S change punches through about 10am and kills it

shark.summary: SharkSmart check pending this refresh — tap to check live detections

days.label: Today
days.note: Clock is ticking — SW offshore holds until roughly 10am, then a S change swings on and turns everything lumpy and building. Go now, not at 11.

swells.label: SSE short-period — wraps poorly into the bay

dee-why.window: Dawn to 9:30am. SW offshore, mid tide filling toward the 12:30pm low. Be out by 9.
alerts: SSE 158° — south quadrant again, Dee Why is under-performing Long Reef by a foot or two
S change ~10am ends the clean window

tip.label: Frontside — Dee Why Point
tip.text: 275 kJ at 9s is modest. The Point is where the SSE finally straightens into a wall — the beachies will be gutless and short. Get the first 90 minutes and don't linger.

swells.label: SSE swell — best exposure of the four

long-reef.window: Best size on the coast this morning. Early, before the S swings cross.
alerts: Wind is cross-shore here even in the AM — less clean than Dee Why

tip.label: Pick of the size
tip.text: Straightest shot at the SSE. A foot or two bigger than Dee Why — worth the paddle if you want actual size.

curl-curl.window: Early only. Banks decide it — have a look before you commit.

tip.label: Middle ground
tip.text: Between Dee Why's size and Manly's shelter. Fine if the banks are on, average if not.

manly.window: Cleanest wind of the four, smallest surf. Longboard/fish call.
alerts: Too small to be worth the drive unless you want a cruise

tip.label: Backside — North Steyne
tip.text: Best wind angle on the coast but only thigh-high. Skip it today unless you're already there.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Energy more than doubles to 662 kJ — solid S swell, but it arrives with the wind. Sheltered corners are the play; the open beaches will be a mess.

dee-why.window: 9–11am while the SW still has a say. Point will be the only orderly thing.
alerts: 662 kJ with a S wind on it — size without shape

long-reef.window: Big and unruly. Experienced only, and even then the wind ruins it.
alerts: Double overhead and cross-shore — heavy, disorganised, not worth it

curl-curl.window: Closing out on the bigger sets. Give it a miss.
alerts: Too much swell for the banks — mostly closeouts

manly.window: The sheltered option Surfline is pointing at. Mid-morning, offshore SW.
alerts: Best conditions-to-size ratio tomorrow — the shadow works in your favour

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the one. SSE fades to a manageable 4–5ft with a near-glassy W offshore at dawn and a NE seabreeze not arriving until afternoon — that's your mid-morning window. Sunday drops to thigh-high with NE–ENE on it.

dee-why.window: Saturday 9am–12pm. W offshore at 3 kph is basically glass. This is the session of the week.
alerts: Consistency only ~62% on Sat — waves come in sets with gaps, be patient

long-reef.window: Saturday early holds the most size as the SSE backs off.
alerts: Sat notably bigger than Sun — don't wait

curl-curl.window: Saturday morning, offshore. Solid backup to Dee Why.

manly.window: Small all weekend. Bottom of the list.
alerts: Shadowed out as the SSE fades — not enough left
